subject: Token lifecycle & auth pattern: post-call recap + next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Gomez <laura@bluelayer.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Token lifecycle & auth pattern: post-call recap + next steps

Hi Laura / Tim,

Great to meet yesterday — thanks for walking us through BlueLayer's integration goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on a secure, low-friction auth approach for the pilot: 

Summary of requirements you shared
- Short-lived tokens for user-facing requests (frontend) to avoid long-lived key exposure
- Server-to-server ingestion (batch) requiring service-account style credentials and KMS integration
- Auditability: request-level logs + rotation events surfaced to your security team
- Support for both API keys (dev/devops) and OAuth 2.0 client flow (customer-facing delegates)

Recommended architecture (high-level)
- Frontend: exchange a short-lived Redwood ephemeral token (TTL 15m) issued by your backend via the OAuth client_credentials or Redwood token exchange endpoint; SDK initializes with ephemeral token and refreshes automatically.
- Backend ingestion: use a Redwood-managed service account credential (JWT signed by customer KMS/HSM or Redwood-hosted KMS if preferred). Rotate keys on a 30-day cadence with immediate revocation on compromise.
- Rotation & revocation: provide an API key rotation webhook to notify your audit pipeline; Redwood can push rotation events to your SIEM via the webhook or CloudEvent.

Tradeoffs we discussed
- API Keys: easiest for early dev, but should be scoped and short-lived for production.
- OAuth/JWT: more setup but best for delegated access and auditability.
- Managed vs. customer KMS: customer KMS gives you key custody (higher compliance bar); Redwood-managed KMS reduces operational overhead.

Action items / proposed next steps
1) We’ll share a short playbook (attached) with SDK snippets for: API key bootstrapping, ephemeral token exchange, service-account JWT examples, and the recommended rotation policy. (See attached redwood-token-lifecycle-playbook.pdf & sdk-auth-snippets.md)
2) You to confirm whether BlueLayer requires customer KMS for the pilot (yes/no) and any compliance checklist items (SOC2 encryption-at-rest, HSM requirement).
3) Quick follow-up technical call: 30 minutes with your infra/security folks + our infra engineer (Rishi). Suggested slots: Mon 11/2 9–11am PT or Wed 11/4 2–4pm PT.

If that aligns, I’ll lock a slot and share a short integration checklist we can use for the pilot kickoff.

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Thanks Ben — this is helpful and maps to what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- For the pilot, we want customer KMS for service account keys (security insistence).
- Our frontend currently uses short-lived cookies; we prefer a token exchange pattern versus embedding API keys in the browser.
- Our security team would like rotation to be automated with a 30-day max rotation window and immediate revocation support.

Tim (cc'd) will join the tech call — he can provide our compliance checklist and confirm internal availability. Tentatively the Mon 11/2 10am PT works for us.

Could you include an example of the token exchange flow (backend->redwood->frontend) in the playbook? Also include a sample CloudEvent body for rotation webhook so our SIEM can parse it.

Appreciate it — looking forward to the call.

Best,

Laura Gomez
Head of Platform Engineering
BlueLayer Financial
laura@bluelayer.com

Laura / Tim — thanks for the quick reply and for confirming customer KMS. Quick note before the call Monday 11/2 10am PT (I’ll send the calendar invite):

What I attached in the playbook
- Token exchange diagram (backend issues short-lived exchange token → frontend calls Redwood with ephemeral token)
- Example code: Node + Python snippets for the exchange, SDK init and automatic refresh (see sdk-auth-snippets.md)
- Rotation webhook sample (CloudEvent JSON) and recommended SIEM parsing keys
- Service-account onboarding flow (CSR/JWT, KMS enrollment steps)

Pilot constraints & recommended defaults
- Ephemeral token TTL: 15 minutes; refresh grant uses a server-side refresh token with 1 hour TTL
- Service-account key rotation: 30-day rotation; automatic rotate + 7-day overlap window to allow graceful rollout
- Audit logs: include token_id, key_version, rotated_by, rotation_time in every rotation webhook event

Decisions we need from BlueLayer before the pilot kickoff
- Confirm KMS provider (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault) and whether you’ll provide HSM-backed keys.
- Confirm whether you want Redwood to host rotation or manage it from your key material.

Next steps (action owners)
- BlueLayer: confirm KMS provider + compliance checklist (Laura / Tim)
- Redwood: send calendar invite + attach final playbook and SDK snippets (Ben)
- Redwood infra: Rishi will prepare a short runbook for the rotation webhook and sample SIEM parsers (Rishi)

If you prefer, I can bring a short demo showing the token exchange in the SDK during the call (10 min). Otherwise we can keep it as a technical Q&A.

Thanks — chat soon.

Ben
